claims.text: minister/assistant to Duke Huan of Qi
wrote resentful and critical verse after castration

translationRepairs: From the time writing was first made, what we can still know of the ancients through the Classics and their commentaries is this: from the ages of Tang and Yu onward, rulers bore formal titles and posthumous names.

From the time writing was first made, what we can still know of the ancients through the Classics and their commentaries is this: for the ages of Tang and Yu and earlier, rulers bore formal titles and posthumous names.
唐虞以上 means the ages of Tang and Yu and earlier (upward in antiquity), not 'onward'; the proposed English restores that temporal direction.

Zhang Yan said, "Laozi was deep and silent, and Confucius regarded him as a teacher. Though not ranked among sages, he surely counts as a great worthy. Wenbo's mother mastered the ritual classics; the sage praised her conduct and later ages took her words as a model—yet she appears in the fourth grade. Tian Dan restored great Qi from the isolated city of Jimo; Lu Zhong was broadly learned yet disdained fame and profit; Lord Lin awed King Qin of Qin and yielded to Lian Po—yet they are placed in the fifth grade. Great Ji practiced sorcery and loved sacrificing to ghosts and spirits; the people of Chen were transformed by her and the state was full of improper cults. The eunuch Mengzi, turning from the great elegant style to preserve himself—after castration, wrote in resentment—yet is placed in the third grade. Lao Ai committed incest at court and threw ritual order into chaos, in deeds too foul to bear hearing—yet he is placed in the seventh grade. Discrepancies and errors are many; I have cited a few to expose the faults. Did he gallop alone across thousands of years, looking on at the various masters while his work remained unfinished, then soon meet the Dou family's disaster—and did that make it turn out this way?"

魯連 is Lu Lian, not Lu Zhong; 秦王 is the King of Qin, not the redundant 'King Qin of Qin'. Both proposed substitutions match the Chinese.

Zhang Yan said: "Laozi was profound and reticent, and Confucius took him as teacher. Though not among the sages, he ought to count as a great worthy. The mother of Wenbo was versed in ritual classics; her conduct won the sage's praise and her words became a model for later ages—yet she is placed in the fourth grade. Tian Dan restored mighty Qi from the lone fortress of Jimo; Lu Zhong was broadly learned yet scorned glory and gain; Lord Lin intimidated King Qin of Qin and yielded ground to Lian Po—yet they are placed in the fifth grade. Great Ji practiced witchcraft and delighted in sacrificing to ghosts and spirits; the people of Chen were transformed by her and the state abounded in licentious worship. The eunuch Mengzi, departing from great elegance to preserve his person—after suffering castration, wrote in resentment and censure—yet is placed in the third grade. Lao Ai committed incest with the sovereign, befouling ritual norms in ways too vile to endure hearing—yet he is placed in the seventh grade. Other discrepancies and errors are numerous; I have raised a few for comparison to expose the mistakes. Did he rush alone through thousands of years, observing the various masters while his work remained incomplete, then soon encounter the Dou family's calamity—which made it come out this way?"

Same naming errors as in the idiomatic field: 魯連 is Lu Lian and 秦王 is the King of Qin; the proposed literal fixes both without other change.
Emperor Ku of the Gaoxin clan
帝嚳 and 高辛氏 are distinct designations; fusing them as 'Emperor Ku Gaoxin' is unclear, and 'Emperor Ku of the Gaoxin clan' correctly separates them.
閼伯 supplies only the name E Bo; the parenthetical '(Bo of Yu)' invents an identification absent from the Chinese.
candidateDispositions: Tang and Yu as era designations in s0001, not the person Yu (禹)
博通 means broadly learned, not a personal name
grade header “wise men”, not a person
大雅 is a section of the Book of Songs
五鳥 / the Five Birds names a collective bird-office group, not one person
五鳩 / the Five Pigeons names a collective pigeon-office group, not one person
三苗 / San Miao names the Three Miao tribal collective, not a single person
